# INV-USD-001, a USD invoice, linked to money that arrived in the CAD bank.
#
# This one really does convert, and only the payer knows at what. The parked
# split's 139.00 CAD is not a conversion of the settlement — it is what stood
# in for the receivable — so there is no rate anywhere in the transaction to
# read one off.
#
# `settled_amount:` is how a payment states what actually landed in the other
# currency, but it belongs to a block that *records* a payment. This block
# links one the book already holds, so what it needs instead is the amounts
# written on the splits themselves.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal naming both currencies and saying what
# to state.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-03-01
    amount: 100
    account: "Assets:Bank"
    txn_guid: "d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90011223"
    txn_split_guid: "f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f900112233445"
